article_title: Hypermobility - the little-known 'bendy disease' that causes pain

tasks.prompt: What central problem does the article highlight about Hypermobility Spectrum Disorders?
options: They can cause wide-ranging pain and fatigue, yet many people wait years for recognition, diagnosis and informed support
They affect only professional athletes and are always diagnosed in childhood
They make joints less flexible and can be cured by one standard medicine
They have detailed national diagnostic guidance and equal access to specialists everywhere
tasks.correct_answer: They can cause wide-ranging pain and fatigue, yet many people wait years for recognition, diagnosis and informed support
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכתבה מדגישה שמדובר בהפרעות רב־מערכתיות שעלולות לגרום לכאב ולעייפות, אך רבות מהן אינן מזוהות במשך שנים.

tasks.prompt: Why do people with HSD often experience muscle fatigue and joint pain?
options: Their bones become permanently shorter
Lax collagen means muscles must work harder to keep unusually mobile joints stable
Their joints have a smaller-than-normal range of motion
Digestive tissue prevents muscles from receiving oxygen
tasks.correct_answer: Lax collagen means muscles must work harder to keep unusually mobile joints stable
tasks.explanation_hebrew: קולגן רפוי ברקמות החיבור מפחית את יציבות המפרקים, ולכן השרירים עובדים קשה יותר כדי לייצב אותם.

tasks.prompt: What average diagnostic delay did the University of Edinburgh research report for hEDS and HSD patients in the UK?
options: Between 19 and 21.7 months
Exactly five years
Between 19 and 21.7 years
More than 58 years for every patient
tasks.explanation_hebrew: המחקר דיווח על המתנה ממוצעת של 19 עד 21.7 שנים לאבחון — לא חודשים.

tasks.prompt: What proportion of diagnosed respondents said they had access to a knowledgeable clinician?
options: More than 90%
Exactly two thirds
Just under one third
Only 13%
tasks.explanation_hebrew: לפי המחקר רק 13% מן המאובחנים דיווחו על גישה לאיש מקצוע שמכיר היטב את ההפרעה.

tasks.prompt: What does “postcode lottery” mean in the discussion of HSD assessment?
options: A medical test based on a patient's postal code
Unequal access to assessment depending on where a person lives
A random method for choosing research participants
A national prize that pays for physiotherapy
tasks.correct_answer: Unequal access to assessment depending on where a person lives
tasks.explanation_hebrew: postcode lottery מתאר מצב שבו השירות או הסיכוי לקבל הערכה משתנים לפי אזור המגורים.

tasks.prompt: What does “imposter syndrome” describe in Luke's account?
options: A condition that makes joints dislocate during sport
A clinical test for hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
Doubt that his pain is legitimate, making him feel he may be exaggerating it
A deliberate attempt to pretend to have another person's diagnosis
tasks.correct_answer: Doubt that his pain is legitimate, making him feel he may be exaggerating it
tasks.explanation_hebrew: כאן imposter syndrome מתאר ספק עצמי: חוסר המידע גורם ללוק לחשוש שהוא מייחס חשיבות מוגזמת לכאב אמיתי.

tasks.prompt: Explain how HSD can affect more than the joints, using at least four examples from the article.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להציג לפחות ארבע השפעות ולחבר אותן למנגנון או לחוויות המתוארות.
expected_points: Muscles work harder to stabilise hypermobile joints, causing fatigue and pain
People may experience clumsiness
Stretchier connective tissue in the digestive system can cause gastrointestinal symptoms
Severe brain fog can affect the ability to work
Standing in queues or on transport can be painful
Symptoms can affect social life and employment
Dislocations and other musculoskeletal problems may occur, particularly with hEDS
Links with autism and ADHD have been established
Symptoms may vary unpredictably from day to day

tasks.prompt: Why do HSD and hEDS often remain undiagnosed or poorly managed for many years?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לשלב גורמים מערכתיים, רפואיים וחברתיים ולא להסתפק בסיבה אחת.
expected_points: Symptoms appear across different body systems and may be treated as unrelated problems
Many patients and professionals have limited awareness of the conditions
There is no dedicated standalone NICE diagnostic guideline
Assessment opportunities vary by location
Women's health has historically been less researched
Under a third of diagnosed respondents said their GP initiated management
Only 13% reported access to a knowledgeable clinician
Patients may doubt themselves or avoid seeking care because information is scarce
Symptoms can fluctuate, making the condition harder to explain

tasks.prompt: Summarise what HSD is, why diagnosis is difficult and how it can be managed.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לכלול הגדרה, מנגנון בסיסי, קשיי אבחון, השפעה יומיומית וגישות טיפול — בלי להציג טיפול כפתרון מוחלט.
expected_points: HSD is a connective-tissue disorder involving a greater-than-normal range of joint motion
Lax collagen can make muscles work harder to stabilise joints
Symptoms include pain, fatigue, clumsiness, digestive problems and sometimes brain fog
Many people wait roughly two decades for diagnosis
Lack of guidance, awareness and knowledgeable clinicians creates unequal access
Symptoms may emerge or worsen after stressors such as puberty or menopause
There is no single magic cure
Physiotherapy can strengthen muscles that support the skeleton
Gentle exercise such as swimming may help some people
Patients need coordinated recognition and support rather than dismissal

tasks.prompt: Write a balanced support plan for a newly diagnosed person with HSD, based on the article.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לנסח תוכנית זהירה באנגלית, להכיר בשונות בין מטופלים ולהשתמש בלפחות ארבע תובנות מן הכתבה.
expected_points: Validate that pain, fatigue and brain fog can be real even when symptoms fluctuate
Seek a clinician knowledgeable about hypermobility when possible
Discuss physiotherapy aimed at strengthening stabilising muscles
Consider gentle exercise such as swimming if individually suitable
Track joint, digestive, fatigue and cognitive symptoms together
Adapt work and daily activities when standing or repetitive tasks cause pain
Avoid presenting physiotherapy as a complete or universal cure
Recognise that stressors may worsen or reveal symptoms
Look for coordinated care and reliable information rather than depending only on social media
